mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate exceeds 4.5%, it indicates a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points within a month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors react to the deteriorating labor market.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 70% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE spikes and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates a weakening economy, which typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised downward.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between GDPC1 decline and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) grows faster than 1% month-over-month, it signals robust economic activity and positive sentiment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between INDPRO growth and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 jobs in a month, combined with a stable or decreasing unemployment rate (UNRATE), signals a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint effect of PAYEMS increase and UNRATE stability/decline on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over two consecutive months signals a strengthening housing market and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between HOUST increase and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% month-over-month signals easing inflationary pressures, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate potential monetary policy easing.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 70% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between CPIAUCSL decrease and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 1% month-over-month signals weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate lower corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between RSAFS decline and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
